'''Apostolos Doxiadis''' ({{IPAc-en|d|ɒ|k|s|i|ˈ|æ|d|ɪ|s}}; {{langx|el|Απόστολος Δοξιάδης}} {{IPA|el|ðoksiˈaðis|}}; born 1953) is a Greek writer. He is best known for his international bestsellers ''[[Uncle Petros and Goldbach's Conjecture]]'' (2000) and ''[[Logicomix]]'' (2009). Most of Doxiadis’ writing in recent decades has been fiction and essays, but he has also written for the theatre and composed librettos for musicals. In the past, he had also worked as a director in theatre and film.

==Early life==
Doxiadis was born in Australia, where his father, the architect [[Constantinos Apostolou Doxiadis]] was working. Soon after his birth, the family returned to [[Athens]] in Greece, where Doxiadis grew up. Though his earliest interests were in poetry, fiction and the theatre, an intense interest in mathematics led Doxiadis to leave school at age fifteen, to attend [[Columbia University]], in [[New York City|New York]], from which he obtained a bachelor's degree in mathematics.<ref>{{cite web |title=Turning Geeks into Superheroes |url=https://www.college.columbia.edu/cct/archive/jul_aug10/bookshelf1 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161226184219/https://www.college.columbia.edu/cct/archive/jul_aug10/bookshelf1 |archive-date=26 December 2016 |website=Columbia College Today}}</ref> He then attended the [[École Pratique des Hautes Études]] in [[Paris]] from which he got a master's degree, with a thesis on the mathematical modelling of the nervous system.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Biography {{!}} Apostolos Doxiadis|url=https://apostolosdoxiadis.com/about/|access-date=16 June 2020|website=apostolosdoxiadis.com|archive-date=22 July 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190722133450/https://www.apostolosdoxiadis.com/about/|url-status=live}}</ref> Before his father's death from ALS in 1975, the resulting family needs made him return to Greece, interrupting his graduate studies. Soon after addressing the needs, Doxiadis gave all his time to his artistic work.

==Work==
===Fiction in English===
In 1998, Doxiadis translated into English, significantly re-working, his third novel, which was published in England in 2000 as ''[[Uncle Petros and Goldbach's Conjecture]]'' (UK publisher: [[Faber and Faber]]; United States publisher: [[Bloomsbury USA]].) The book became an international bestseller, and has been published to date in more than thirty-five languages. It has received the praise of, among others, Nobel laureate [[John Forbes Nash Jr.|John Nash]], British mathematician [[Sir Michael Atiyah]], critic [[George Steiner]] and neurologist [[Oliver Sacks]]. ''Uncle Petros'' is one of the ''[[1001 Books You Must Read Before You Die]]''.<ref>http://1001beforeyoudie.com {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140110124836/http://1001beforeyoudie.com/ |date=10 January 2014 }}</ref>
  
Doxiadis' next project, which took over five years to complete, was the graphic novel ''[[Logicomix]]'' (2009), a number one bestseller on the [[The New York Times Best Seller list|''New York Times'' Best Seller list]] and an international bestseller, already published in over twenty languages. ''Logicomix'' was co-authored with computer scientist [[Christos Papadimitriou]], with art work by [[Alecos Papadatos]] (pencils) and Annie Di Donna (colour). Renowned comics historian and critic [[R. C. Harvey]], in the ''[[Comics Journal]]'', called ''Logicomix'' "a tour-de-force" a "virtuoso performance",<ref>{{cite web |url=http://classic.tcj.com/history/logicomix-a-tour-de-force/ |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130916065000/http://classic.tcj.com/history/logicomix-a-tour-de-force/ |archive-date=16 September 2013 |title=Logicomix, A Tour de Force « The Comics Journal}}</ref> while ''[[The Sunday Times]]''{{'}} [[Bryan Appleyard]] called it "probably the best and certainly the most extraordinary graphic novel" he has read. ''Logicomix'' is one of [[Paul Gravett]]'s ''1001 Comics You Must Read Before you Die''. <ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.paulgravett.com/index.php/1001_comics/ |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130715234908/http://www.paulgravett.com/index.php/1001_comics |archive-date=15 July 2013 |title=Paul Gravett {{!}} 1001 Comics}}</ref>

===Fiction in Greek===
Doxiadis began to write in Greek. His first published work was ''A Parallel Life'' (''Βίος Παράλληλος'', 1985), a novella set in the monastic communities of 4th-century CE Egypt, dealing with the conflict between faith and temptation. His first novel, ''Makavettas'' (''Μακαβέττας'', 1988), recounted the adventures of a fictional power-hungry colonel at the time of the [[Greek military junta of 1967–1974]]. Written in a tongue-in-cheek imitation of Greek folk military memoirs, such as that of [[Yannis Makriyannis]], it follows the plot of Shakespeare's ''[[Macbeth]]'', of which the eponymous hero's name is a Hellenized form. Doxiadis next novel, ''Uncle Petros and Goldbach's Conjecture'' (''Ο Θείος Πέτρος και η Εικασία του Γκόλντμπαχ'', 1992), was the first long work of fiction whose plot takes place in the world of pure mathematics research. The novella ''The Three Little Men'' (''{{lang|el|Τα Τρία Ανθρωπάκια|italic=unset}}'', 1998) was later expanded into the longer novel ''The Three Little Pigs'', which reworks motifs from the "Three Little Pigs" fairy tale in a crime narrative, a morality tale set in the world of the Italian Mafia.<ref name="CrimeFictionLover2016">{{cite web |last=Megraw |first=Jeremy |title=Three Little Pigs: A Story by Apostles Doxiadis |url=https://crimefictionlover.com/2016/03/three-little-pigs-a-story/ |website=Crime Fiction Lover |date=25 March 2016 |access-date=19 February 2026 |language=en |archive-date=8 February 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260208084752/https://crimefictionlover.com/2016/03/three-little-pigs-a-story/ |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name="ProtothemaBio">{{cite news |title=Απόστολος Δοξιάδης εκ βαθέων: «Ερασιτέχνης επαναστάτης» |url=https://www.protothema.gr/culture/books/article/844998/apostolos-doxiadis-ek-vatheon-erasitehnis-epanastatis/ |work=Πρώτο Θέμα |date=6 December 2018 |access-date=19 February 2026 |language=el |quote=Έγραψε τα πεζογραφήματα [...] Τα Τρία Ανθρωπάκια (Καστανιώτης, 1998) |archive-date=27 August 2025 novel has appeared in translation, including Spanish as ''Tres cerditos'' ([[Alianza Editorial]], 2017),<ref name="TresCerditos2017">{{cite book |last=Doxiadis |first=Apostolos |title=Tres cerditos |publisher=Alianza Editorial |year=2017 |isbn=978-84-9104-813-8 |language=es}}</ref> Italian as ''Tre piccoli porcellini: tre fratelli, un gangster, una maledizione'' (Bompiani),<ref February 2026 |language=it}}</ref> and German as ''Des Menschen Wolf'' (Tropen, 2017).<ref name="DesMenschenWolf2017">{{cite book |last=Doxiadis |first=Apostolos |title=Des Menschen Wolf Doxiadis's upcoming novel, ''Bluedog'' (''{{lang|el|Γαλανόσκυλος|italic=unset}}''), is scheduled for publication on 19 March 2026.<ref name="AthensVoice2025">{{cite web |title=Γαλανόσκυλος: Ο Απόστολος Δοξιάδης επιστρέφει με ένα μυθιστόρημα |url=https://www.athensvoice.gr/politismos/vivlio/937722/galanoskulos-o-apostolos-doxiadis-epistrefei-me-ena-muthistorima/ |website=Athens Voice |date=11 December 2025 |language=el |access-date=19 February 2026 |archive-date=24 January 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260124015659/https://www.athensvoice.gr/politismos/vivlio/937722/galanoskulos-o-apostolos-doxiadis-epistrefei-me-ena-muthistorima/ |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name="Athinorama2025">{{cite web |title=Στις Εκδόσεις Ψυχογιός με νέο μυθιστόρημα ο Απόστολος Δοξιάδης |url=https://www.athinorama.gr/texnes/3064668/stis-ekdoseis-psuxogios-o-apostolos-doxiadis/ |website=Athinorama |date=11 December 2025 |language=el |access-date=19 February 2026 |archive-date=11 January 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260111025526/https://www.athinorama.gr/texnes/3064668/stis-ekdoseis-psuxogios-o-apostolos-doxiadis/ |url-status=live }}</ref> Blending realistic and fantastic elements, the narrative alternates between 1990s Greece and the 1940s during the Axis occupation. Thematically, it explores the contrast between modernity and tradition.

===Non-fiction in Greek===
In ''Amateur revolutionary'' (''{{lang|el|Ερασιτέχνης επαναστάτης|italic=unset}}'', 2018), an autobiographical narrative described as a "personal myth-history", Doxiadis recounts his life from childhood to early adulthood, focusing on his political formation during the years of the Greek military dictatorship.<ref name="Lifo2018">{{cite web |title=Ο Απόστολος Δοξιάδης μιλά ατρόμητα στη LiFO για τους μύθους της γενιάς του |url=https://www.lifo.gr/culture/vivlio/o-apostolos-doxiadis-mila-atromita-sti-lifo-gia-toys-mythoys-tis-genias-toy |website=LiFO |date=21 November 2018 |language=el |access-date=19 February 2026 |archive-date=27 March 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260327055334/https://www.lifo.gr/culture/vivlio/o-apostolos-doxiadis-mila-atromita-sti-lifo-gia-toys-mythoys-tis-genias-toy |url-status=live }}</ref>

He followed his first direct memoir with a work of autofiction, ''The phone call that never was'' (''{{lang|el|Το τηλεφώνημα που δεν έγινε|italic=unset}}'', 2022). The narrative is centered on his first artistic work in his adolescence and the conflict with his father it led to, framed by a contemporary, partly fictional inquiry into the meaning of that work.<ref name="KathimeriniInterview2022">{{cite news |title=Ο Απόστολος Δοξιάδης στην «Κ»: Το χρονικό μιας ψυχικής αναζήτησης |url=https://www.kathimerini.gr/opinion/interviews/561904750/o-apostolos-doxiadis-stin-k-to-chroniko-mias-psychikis-anazitisis/ |work=Kathimerini |date=13 June 2022 |language=el |access-date=19 February 2026 |archive-date=12 June 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220612183042/https://www.kathimerini.gr/opinion/interviews/561904750/o-apostolos-doxiadis-stin-k-to-chroniko-mias-psychikis-anazitisis/ |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name="Kotzia2022">{{cite news |last=Kotzia |first=Elisavet |title=Υπογραμμίζοντας το ανεκπλήρωτο |url=https://www.kathimerini.gr/culture/books/561970993/ypogrammizontas-to-anekpliroto/ |work=Kathimerini |date=30 June 2022 |language=el |access-date=19 February 2026 |archive-date=26 February 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240226113111/https://www.kathimerini.gr/culture/books/561970993/ypogrammizontas-to-anekpliroto/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

===Theatre and cinema===

He has written two plays for the theatre. The first was a full-length shadow-puppet play with music and songs, ''The Tragical History of Jackson Pollock, Abstract Expressionist'' (1999), in English, of which he also designed and directed the Athens performance.The music is By Dimitris Papadimitriou.<ref name="JPYouTube">{{cite AV media |title=The Tragical History of Jackson Pollock, Abstract Expressionist |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=BJMyQ4Bkiow |publisher=Apostolos Doxiadis |date=20 August 2012 |medium=Video |access-date=19 February 2026}}</ref> In this play, Doxiadis realized some of his views on "epic theatre", in other words, a theatre based on storytelling, also influenced by the techniques of Greek shadow theatre [[Karagiozis]], the Japanese puppet theatre [[Bunraku]] and other traditional Asian forms.<ref name="DoxiadisTheater">{{cite web |title=Storytelling and Theatre: The Tragical History of Jackson Pollock, Abstract Expressionist |url=https://apostolosdoxiadis.com/theater/the-tragical-history-of-jackson-pollock-abstract-expressionist/ |website=Apostolos Doxiadis |access-date=19 February 2026 |archive-date=22 April 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240422005055/https://apostolosdoxiadis.com/theater/the-tragical-history-of-jackson-pollock-abstract-expressionist/ |url-status=live }}</ref> His second play, ''Incompleteness'' (2005), is an imaginary account of the last seventeen days in the life of the great logician [[Kurt Gödel]], which Gödel spent in a [[Princeton, New Jersey]], hospital, refusing to eat out of fear that he was being poisoned. The play was staged in Athens in 2006 as ''Dekati Evdomi Nyhta'' (Seventeenth Night) with the actor Yorgos Kotanidis in the role of Kurt Gödel.<ref name="KotanidisERT">{{cite news |title=Πέθανε ο Γιώργος Κοτανίδης |url=https://www.ertnews.gr/eidiseis/ellada/kinonia/pethane-o-giorgos-kotanidis/ |work=ERT News |date=28 January 2020 |language=el |access-date=19 February 2026}}</ref>

In the early stages of his career, before focusing full-time on writing, Doxiadis worked in professional theatre in Athens as a director and translator,<ref name="Guardian2001">{{cite news |last=Lezard |first=Nicholas |author-link=Nicholas Lezard |title=Number crunching |url=https://www.theguardian.com/books/2001/mar/03/scienceandnature.nicholaslezard |work=The Guardian |date=3 March 2001 |access-date=19 February 2026}}</ref> translating among other plays Shakespeare's ''Hamlet'' and Eugene O’Neill’s ''Mourning Becomes Electra''.<ref name="Guardian2001" /> For the Greek National Theatre, he also translated and adapted, in a mixed form of prose and songs, Shakespeare's ''A Midsummer Night's Dream'', with music by Dimitris Papadimitriou.<ref name="NationalTheatreDream1999">{{cite web |title=Όνειρο καλοκαιρινής νύχτας (1999) |url=https://www.nt-archive.gr/play/596 |website=Ψηφιοποιημένο Αρχείο Εθνικού Θεάτρου |publisher=Εθνικό Θέατρο |language=el |access-date=20 February 2026}}</ref>

Doxiadis has also written and directed two feature-length films, in Greek, ''Underground Passage'' (''Υπόγεια Διαδρομή'', 1983) and ''Terirem'' (''Τεριρέμ'', 1987). The latter won the [[CICAE]] (International Confederation of Art Cinemas) prize for Best Film in the 1988 [[Berlin International Film Festival]].

===Scholarship===

Doxiadis has an intense interest in logic, cognitive psychology and rhetoric, as well as the theoretical study of narrative. <ref>Some of his published papers are reprinted here: {{cite web|url=http://www.apostolosdoxiadis.com/en/index.php?option%3Dcom_content%26view%3Darticle%26id%3D189%26Itemid%3D70 |title=Proofs and Stories |accessdate=18 October 2012 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20120105053729/http://www.apostolosdoxiadis.com/en/index.php?option=com_content&view=article&id=189&Itemid=70 |archivedate=5 January 2012 }}</ref> In 2007, he organized, with mathematician [[Barry Mazur]], a meeting on the theoretical investigation of the relationship of mathematics and narrative, whose proceedings were published as ''Circles Disturbed: The Interplay of Mathematics and Narrative'' (2012).<ref>{{Cite book|url = http://press.princeton.edu/titles/9764.html|isbn = 9780691149042|title = Circles Disturbed|date = 18 March 2012|last1 = Doxiadis|first1 = Apostolos|last2 = Mazur|first2 = Barry|publisher = Princeton University Press|archive-date = 8 November 2012|access-date = 18 October 2012|archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20121108015235/http://press.princeton.edu/titles/9764.html|url-status = live}}</ref> Doxiadis has lectured extensively on his theoretical interests.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://royalsociety.org/exhibitions/one-culture/apostolos-doxiadis/|title=Welcome to the Royal Society &#124; Royal Society|access-date=18 October 2012|archive-date=6 January 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120106220550/http://royalsociety.org/exhibitions/one-culture/apostolos-doxiadis/|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://mediasite.rhul.ac.uk/rhul/SilverlightPlayer/Default.aspx?peid%3D0422442741e14f90a3cc8a098b14ab051d |title=Dabis Lecture - Apostolos Doxiadis 'From Mimesis to Aristotle for Screenwriters- and back'_001 |accessdate=18 October 2012 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20110912161456/http://mediasite.rhul.ac.uk/rhul/SilverlightPlayer/Default.aspx?peid=0422442741e14f90a3cc8a098b14ab051d |archivedate=12 September 2011 }}</ref> Doxiadis' recent work has led him to formulate a theory about the development of deductive proof in [[classical Greece]], which lays emphasis on influences from pre-existing patterns in narrative and, especially, [[Archaic Greece#Poetry|Archaic Age poetry]].<ref>An earlier draft of a write-up of some of these ideas can be found at https://www.academia.edu/3222520/A_Streetcar_Named_among_Other_Things_Proof {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181215122157/https://www.academia.edu/3222520/A_Streetcar_Named_among_Other_Things_Proof |date=15 December 2018 }}</ref> 

Doxiadis traces the origins of deductive mathematical proof in classical Greece, arguing that rhetorical concepts—particularly forensic rhetoric shaped by narrativity and forms of poetic storytelling—affected both the macrostructure and microstructure of early Greek proofs.<ref name="DoxiadisCircles2012">{{cite book |last=Doxiadis |first=Apostolos |chapter=A Streetcar Named (among Other Things) Proof: From Storytelling to Geometry, via Poetry and Rhetoric |editor-last=Doxiadis |editor-first=Apostolos |editor-last2=Mazur |editor-first2=Barry |title=Circles Disturbed: The Interplay of Mathematics and Narrative |location=Princeton, NJ |publisher=Princeton University Press |year=2012 |pages=281–388 |isbn=978-0-691-14904-2 |doi=10.23943/princeton/9780691149042.003.0010 |url=https://doi.org/10.23943/princeton/9780691149042.003.0010 |access-date=19 February 2026}}</ref>

==Public commentary and political engagement==

===Military dictatorship period===
In his autobiographical work ''Amateur revolutionary'' (''{{lang|el|Ερασιτέχνης επαναστάτης|italic=unset}}'', 2018), Doxiadis describes in detail his involvement in the resistance to the [[Greek junta]] (1967–1974) through his participation in the clandestine anti-dictatorship cell of the student organisation associated with the [[Communist Party of Greece (Interior)]].<ref name="BookPressErasitechnis">{{cite web |title=Το απομυθοποιητικό βλέμμα μιας προσωπικής μυθιστόρησης |url=https://bookpress.gr/home/bookpress/www/www/kritikes/biografies/10085-doxiadis-apostolos-ikaros-erasitechnis-epanastatis-soumas |website=Book Press |date=17 April 2019 |language=el |access-date=19 February 2026}}</ref> In his memoir he adopts a critical perspective on aspects of the Greek Left, including bureaucracy and doctrinaire communist politics.<ref name="BookPressErasitechnis" /><ref name="KathimeriniTsompanakos2018">{{cite news |title=Απόστολος Δοξιάδης: Αμαρτωλές σκέψεις ενός τσομπανάκου |url=https://www.kathimerini.gr/culture/books/997597/apostolos-doxiadis-amartoles-skepseis-enos-tsompanakoy/ |work=Kathimerini |date=10 December 2018 |language=el |access-date=19 February 2026 |archive-date=14 July 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240714223347/https://www.kathimerini.gr/culture/books/997597/apostolos-doxiadis-amartoles-skepseis-enos-tsompanakoy/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

===Greek financial crisis===
During the Greek financial crisis, Doxiadis intervened in public debate through essays and opinion pieces. In an article published immediately after the [[2015 Greek bailout referendum]], he criticized what he described as populist narratives and misinformation surrounding the vote.<ref name="DoxiadisKathimerini2015">{{cite news |last=Doxiadis |first=Apostolos |title=Αποψη: Τα συνεχή μεγάλα ψέματα |url=https://www.kathimerini.gr/politics/822397/apopsi-ta-synechi-megala-psemata/ |work=Kathimerini |date=6 July 2015 |language=el |access-date=19 February 2026}}</ref> In a 2016 lecture at Oxford University's South East European Studies programme (SEESOX), Doxiadis argued that a strand of Greek public intellectuals of the political centre, of which he was one, coalesced around opposition to populism and support for the European project during the period 2012–2015.<ref name="OxfordTalks2016">{{cite web |title=SEESOX Seminar Series: Unpopular Voices: Greek public intellectuals of the political centre during the Crisis |url=https://talks.ox.ac.uk/talks/series/id/050b2ec0-4c3c-4e48-96d9-f6fb6fa8f266 |website=Oxford Talks |publisher=University of Oxford |date=25 April 2016 |access-date=19 February 2026 |archive-date=17 April 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250417211923/https://talks.ox.ac.uk/talks/series/id/050b2ec0-4c3c-4e48-96d9-f6fb6fa8f266 |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name="DoxiadisSEESOXVideo">{{cite AV media |people=Apostolos Doxiadis |title=Unpopular Voices: Greek public intellectuals of the political Centre during the Crisis |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=mgmNKwKlos4 |date=17 June 2017 |medium=Video |location=St Antony's College, Oxford |access-date=19 February 2026}}</ref>

===The case of the eight Turkish officers===
After the failed coup attempt in Turkey in July 2016, eight Turkish military personnel flew to Greece by helicopter and applied for asylum.<ref name="ReutersEuronews2018">{{cite news |title=Greek committee grants asylum to Turkish soldier - judicial sources |url=https://www.euronews.com/2018/07/05/greek-committee-grants-asylum-to-turkish-soldier-judicial-sources |work=Euronews (Reuters) |date=5 July 2018 |access-date=19 February 2026 |archive-date=5 July 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180705134838/http://www.euronews.com/2018/07/05/greek-committee-grants-asylum-to-turkish-soldier-judicial-sources |url-status=live }}</ref> In December 2016, an Athens court approved extradition for three of the eight, a decision subsequently challenged in Greece’s judicial process.<ref name="DWExtradition2016">{{cite news |title=Greek court agrees to extradite three Turkish officers |url=https://www.dw.com/en/greek-court-agrees-to-extradite-three-turkish-officers/a-36662488 |work=Deutsche Welle |date=6 December 2016 |access-date=19 February 2026 |archive-date=7 February 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250207222339/https://www.dw.com/en/greek-court-agrees-to-extradite-three-turkish-officers/a-36662488 |url-status=live }}</ref> Greece’s Supreme Court (Areios Pagos) later ruled in January 2017 against extraditing the eight, citing concerns about fair-trial guarantees in Turkey.<ref name="GuardianExtradition2017">{{cite news |title=Greek court turns down extradition request for eight Turkish officers |url=https://www.theguardian.com/world/2017/jan/26/greek-court-turns-down-extradition-request-eight-turkish-officers-ankara-failed-coup |work=The Guardian |date=26 January 2017 |access-date=19 February 2026}}</ref><ref name="DWAreiosPagos2017">{{cite news |title=Greece's top court roils Turkey over coup extradition |url=https://www.dw.com/en/greeces-top-court-roils-turkey-over-coup-extradition/a-37292376 |work=Deutsche Welle |date=26 January 2017 |access-date=19 February 2026 |archive-date=21 August 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250821022632/https://www.dw.com/en/greeces-top-court-roils-turkey-over-coup-extradition/a-37292376 |url-status=live }}</ref>

The asylum process continued through administrative proceedings. In 2018, the Council of State (Greece’s highest administrative court) upheld the refugee status of one of the servicemen, rejecting the government’s arguments against granting protection.<ref name="EDAL1694_2018">{{cite web |title=Greece - Council of State, Decision 1694/2018, 21 August 2018 |url=https://www.asylumlawdatabase.eu/en/content/greece-council-state-decision-16942018-21-august-2018 |website=European Database of Asylum Law (EDAL) |access-date=19 February 2026 |archive-date=30 March 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260330142311/https://www.asylumlawdatabase.eu/en/content/greece-council-state-decision-16942018-21-august-2018 |url-status=live }}</ref> Reuters reporting in 2018 described asylum being granted to one of the group by a Greek committee, while noting that court decisions on extradition were based on fair-trial concerns.<ref name="ReutersEuronews2018" /> Reuters reporting in 2019 referred to the eight as having been granted asylum in Greece.<ref name="ReutersEuronews2019">{{cite news |title=Erdogan says he expects Greece to return eight Turkish soldiers with coup links |url=https://www.euronews.com/2019/02/05/erdogan-says-expects-greece-to-return-eight-turkish-soldiers-with-coup-links |work=Euronews (Reuters) |date=5 February 2019 |access-date=19 February 2026 |archive-date=10 May 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220510220016/https://www.euronews.com/2019/02/05/erdogan-says-expects-greece-to-return-eight-turkish-soldiers-with-coup-links |url-status=live }}</ref>

During the proceedings, Doxiadis publicly intervened with opinion pieces in the Greek press, opposing extradition and arguing for the officers' protection.<ref name="KathimeriniDoxiadis2016">{{cite news |last=Doxiadis |first=Apostolos |title=Οκτώ ψυχές αφημένες σε ελληνικές συνειδήσεις |url=https://www.kathimerini.gr/opinion/889295/okto-psyches-afimenes-se-ellinikes-syneidiseis/ |work=Kathimerini |date=26 December 2016 |language=el |access-date=19 February 2026 |archive-date=21 December 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241221170743/https://www.kathimerini.gr/opinion/889295/okto-psyches-afimenes-se-ellinikes-syneidiseis/ |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name="AthensVoiceDoxiadis2016">{{cite web |title=Απ. Δοξιάδης: «Γιατί παίρνω την υπόθεση των 8 Τούρκων προσωπικά» |url=https://www.athensvoice.gr/epikairotita/politiki-oikonomia/335077/ap-doxiadis-giati-pairno-tin-ypothesi-ton-8-toyrkon/ |website=Athens Voice |date=25 December 2016 |language=el |access-date=19 February 2026 |archive-date=21 August 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250821011941/https://www.athensvoice.gr/epikairotita/politiki-oikonomia/335077/ap-doxiadis-giati-pairno-tin-ypothesi-ton-8-toyrkon/ |url-status=live }}</ref> Writing in ''Athens Voice'', [[Ireni Agapidaki]] noted that Doxiadis "shouldered the burden" of the defense of the eight officers in the public sphere.<ref name="AgapidakiEight2018">{{cite web |last=Agapidaki |first=Irene |title=Δύο μαθήματα που πήρα από την υπόθεση των Οκτώ |url=https://www.athensvoice.gr/epikairotita/politiki-oikonomia/446033/dyo-mathimata-poy-pira-apo-tin-ypothesi-ton-okto/ |website=Athens Voice |date=25 May 2018 |language=el |access-date=19 February 2026 |archive-date=10 June 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260610061455/https://www.athensvoice.gr/epikairotita/politiki-oikonomia/446033/dyo-mathimata-poy-pira-apo-tin-ypothesi-ton-okto/ |url-status=live }}</ref> He also wrote on the case in the international press, including an op-ed in ''The Wall Street Journal'' on the rule-of-law implications for Europe.<ref name="WSJDoxiadis2017">{{cite news |last=Doxiadis |first=Apostolos |title=Turkey's Coup and Europe's Rule of Law |url=https://www.wsj.com/articles/turkeys-coup-and-europes-rule-of-law-1483645331 |work=The Wall Street Journal |date=5 January 2017 |access-date=19 February 2026 |archive-date=29 March 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230329231818/https://www.wsj.com/articles/turkeys-coup-and-europes-rule-of-law-1483645331 |url-status=live }}</ref> In March 2018, he was examined as a witness in appellate-court proceedings concerning an extradition request.<ref name="ToVima2018">{{cite news |title=Greek appellate court: Third rejection of request for extradition of eight Turkish army officers |url=https://www.tovima.gr/2018/03/16/international/greek-appellate-court-third-rejection-of-request-for-extradition-of-eight-turkish-army-officers/amp/ |work=To Vima |date=16 March 2018 |access-date=19 February 2026}}</ref> Writing in ''The Guardian'', columnist Nick Cohen described Doxiadis, for his role in the case, as a "Greek Zola".<ref name="CohenGuardian2017">{{cite news |last=Cohen |first=Nick |title=Fate of eight Turkish airmen is an acid test for democracy |url=https://www.theguardian.com/commentisfree/2017/jan/22/fate-eight-turkish-airmen-acid-test-for-democracy |work=The Guardian |date=22 January 2017 |access-date=19 February 2026}}</ref>

===Protection of unaccompanied minors===

In November 2019, Prime Minister Kyriakos Mitsotakis announced the programme “No Child Alone” (''{{lang|el|Κανένα παιδί μόνο|italic=unset}}'') for the care of unaccompanied children in Greece and appointed Irene Agapidaki as national coordinator, with Doxiadis named as a representative of civil society.<ref>name="HRW2020">{{cite news |title=Greece: Free Unaccompanied Migrant Children |url=https://www.hrw.org/news/2020/04/14/greece-free-unaccompanied-migrant-children |work=Human Rights Watch |date=14 April 2020 |access-date=19 February 2026 |archive-date=3 March 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260303171223/https://www.hrw.org/news/2020/04/14/greece-free-unaccompanied-migrant-children |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name="LiFOAgapidaki2019">{{cite web |title=Αγαπηδάκη και Δοξιάδης στο σχέδιο «Κανένα παιδί μόνο» για τα ασυνόδευτα προσφυγόπουλα |url=https://www.lifo.gr/now/greece/agapidaki-kai-doxiadis-sto-shedio-kanena-paidi-mono-gia-ta-asynodeyta-prosfygopoyla |website=LiFO |date=24 November 2019 |language=el |access-date=19 February 2026 |archive-date=6 August 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250806123818/https://www.lifo.gr/now/greece/agapidaki-kai-doxiadis-sto-shedio-kanena-paidi-mono-gia-ta-asynodeyta-prosfygopoyla |url-status=live }}</ref>

===Other advocacy===

In 2019, during a high-profile extradition case involving an Iranian woman and her young daughter, Doxiadis publicised the case and called for support. He also appeared as a witness for her defence in the Supreme Court.<ref name="ProtoThemaDoxiadis2019">{{cite web |title=Την υπόθεση της Σαραρέ Κχαντεμί και της εξάχρονης κόρης της δημοσιοποιεί ο συγγραφέας Απόστολος Δοξιάδης… |url=https://www.protothema.gr/greece/article/934107/apostolos-doxiadis-o-areios-pagos-to-mono-teihos-dikaiosunis-gia-mia-anuperaspisti-irani-kai-to-paidi-tis/ |website=Proto Thema |date=16 October 2019 |language=el |access-date=19 February 2026 |archive-date=15 December 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251215051047/https://www.protothema.gr/greece/article/934107/apostolos-doxiadis-o-areios-pagos-to-mono-teihos-dikaiosunis-gia-mia-anuperaspisti-irani-kai-to-paidi-tis/ |url-status=live }}</ref> The Supreme Court overturned an extradition order in the case, citing risks upon return.<ref name="EkathimeriniIranian2019">{{cite news |title=Supreme Court upholds Iranian woman's appeal against extradition |url=https://www.ekathimerini.com/news/245918/supreme-court-upholds-iranian-woman-s-appeal-against-extradition/ |work=eKathimerini.com |date=29 October 2019 |access-date=19 February 2026 |archive-date=5 March 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240305080148/https://www.ekathimerini.com/news/245918/supreme-court-upholds-iranian-woman-s-appeal-against-extradition/ |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name="EDALIranian2019">{{cite web |title=Greece - Supreme Civil and Criminal Court - Decision 1690/2019, 29 October 2019 |url=https://www.asylumlawdatabase.eu/el/case-law/greece-supreme-civil-and-criminal-court-decision-16902019-29-october-2019 |website=European Database of Asylum Law (EDAL) |language=el |access-date=19 February 2026 |archive-date=30 March 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260330045635/https://www.asylumlawdatabase.eu/el/case-law/greece-supreme-civil-and-criminal-court-decision-16902019-29-october-2019 |url-status=live }}</ref>

===Political views===

In a 2025 public conversation, Doxiadis said, "The left-wingers call me right-wing, while the right-wingers call me left-wing." He described himself as “a liberal”, while distinguishing this from “neoliberalism”. In terms of social welfare and justice, he described himself as "center-left".<ref name="Protagon2025">{{cite web |title=Ο Απόστολος Δοξιάδης προσκεκλημένος του Ηλία Κανέλλη στο Ωδείο Αθηνών |url=https://www.protagon.gr/epikairotita/o-apostolos-doksiadis-proskeklimenos-tou-ilia-kanelli-sto-wdeio-athinwn-44343242951 |website=Protagon.gr |date=23 October 2025 |language=el |access-date=19 February 2026 |archive-date=23 October 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251023200527/https://www.protagon.gr/epikairotita/o-apostolos-doksiadis-proskeklimenos-tou-ilia-kanelli-sto-wdeio-athinwn-44343242951 |url-status=live }}</ref>

===Thales + Friends===

Doxiadis is a co-founder of THALES + FRIENDS (''{{lang|el|ΘΑΛΗΣ + ΦΙΛΟΙ|italic=unset}}''), a Greece-based, volunteer non-profit initiative founded in 2005 that supports the creation of reading groups (including school-based groups) and related activities exploring links between mathematics/science and narrative.<ref name="ThalesFriendsProsopa">{{cite web |title=Πρόσωπα |url=https://thalesandfriends.org/el/prosopa/ |website=ΘΑΛΗΣ + ΦΙΛΟΙ |language=el |access-date=19 February 2026 |archive-date=11 December 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251211112948/https://thalesandfriends.org/el/prosopa/ |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name="ThalesFriendsSkopos">{{cite web |title=Σκοπός και δραστηριότητες |url=https://thalesandfriends.org/el/prosopa/skopos/ |website=ΘΑΛΗΣ + ΦΙΛΟΙ |language=el |access-date=19 February 2026 |archive-date=11 December 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251211113207/https://thalesandfriends.org/el/prosopa/skopos/ |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name="AthensCultureNetThales">{{cite web |title=Thales + Friends |url=https://www.athensculturenet.com/en/acn-affiliate-organization/thales-friends |website=Athens Culture Net |access-date=19 February 2026 |archive-date=23 January 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260123180300/https://www.athensculturenet.com/en/acn-affiliate-organization/thales-friends |url-status=live }}</ref>

==Awards and honours==
For ''Uncle Petros and Goldbach's Conjecture'', Doxiadis was the first recipient of the Premio Peano<ref>[http://www.subalpinamathesis.unito.it/attivita/premiopeano.php Associazione Subalpina Mathesis – Premio Peano] {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121119213218/http://www.subalpinamathesis.unito.it/attivita/premiopeano.php |date=19 November 2012 }}</ref> and short-listed for the [[Prix Médicis]]. For ''Logicomix'' he has earned numerous awards, among them the [[Bertrand Russell]] Society Award, the Royal Booksellers Association Award (the Netherlands), the New Atlantic Booksellers Award (US), the Prix Tangente (France), the Premio Carlo Boscarato (Italy), the Comicdom Award (Greece). It was chosen as "Book of the Year" by ''[[Time (magazine)|Time]]'', ''[[Publishers Weekly]]'', ''[[The Washington Post]]'', ''[[The Financial Times]]'', ''[[The Globe and Mail]]'', and other publications.
